Subject: EdSurge renewal — initial order form and a couple MSA asks

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the quick turnaround on numbers. Attaching our latest internal order form (EdSurge_OrderForm_v3.docx) and a short note on two MSA items we need to confirm before we can route to procurement: 

1) Term alignment: our finance team wants a 24-month term that auto-renews for optional 12-month periods; can you confirm Redwood can support that timing?
2) Data residency carve: we need the clause clarified that logs older than 30 days are archived in the US region only.

Also flagging a potential ask from our security folks on audit log retention — they may come back with a short questionnaire this week. Please loop in your legal and ops folks so we can keep this moving.

Attaching the order form now. If we can get a clean redline of the MSA + order form by Friday (10/23) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Head of Ops, EdSurge

Subject: Re: EdSurge renewal — initial order form and a couple MSA asks

Sara — thanks, received. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

On term: we can offer a 24-month firm term with an optional 12-month auto-renew thereafter. Finance-side note: pricing tiers will be fixed for the 24 months, bump TBD on renewals; Ben will include escalation examples in the order form.

On data residency: we can confirm primary storage and audit logs are retained in the US region for >30 days, but need legal to draft precise language for archival access and e-discovery carveouts.

Security questionnaire: understood — Naomi, please watch for incoming questionnaire and prep the standard SOC2 attestation pack.

Kimberly — can you take the attached EdSurge_OrderForm_v3 and the MSA, apply Redwood's standard redline around term language and the data residency paragraph, and produce a marked copy by end of day Thursday? If there are any hard stops from legal (e.g., indemnity/insurance changes), flag them to me so I can raise with the customer.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberley to redline MSA + order form (target: Thu 10/22 EOD)
- Ben to add pricing escalation examples to order form v3 (target: Wed 10/21)
- Naomi to prep SOC2 evidence bundle if requested (ongoing)

Happy to jump on a 20-min touchpoint if it helps.

Best,

Subject: Re: EdSurge renewal — initial order form and a couple MSA asks

Thanks for the context — I reviewed the attached MSA and the order form and pushed a few focused edits. Summary of the redline rationale below; full redline attached (MSA_Redline_Markus_v2.docx).

Summary of edits / asks from legal:
- Term: Accepting 24-month firm term + 12-month auto-renew, subject to mutual pricing notice 60 days prior to renewal. Inserted language at Section 2.1.
- Data residency / logs: Clarified archive vs. primary storage. We will confirm that logs older than 30 days are archived in the US, but we cannot restrict support or e-discovery to US-only without prior written agreement; added an exception for legal holds and emergency access across regions.
- Indemnity: Edits narrow Redwood's indemnity exposure for third-party IP claims to exceptions where customer provides infringing materials — please confirm if EdSurge can accept this carveout.
- SLA credits: tightened SLO credit calculation language to match our standard exhibit; EdSurge had a higher credit % in the order form that I adjusted down to Redwood standard.

Open items for commercial to confirm with customer:
1) Pricing tiers freeze for the 24 months vs. scheduled uplift on the auto-renew — Ben will confirm the exact phrasing and any uplift caps.
2) Audit log retention access: we need confirmation on whether EdSurge expects encrypted exports or Redwood-provided access; if they want exports, there will be a nominal export fee.

I attached the redline and a brief one-pager with proposed language for each open item. If Sara/legal can accept the indemnity carveout and the access carve on logs, we should be able to move to procurement signoff next week.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_Redline_Markus_v2.docx
From: EdSurge Legal <legal@edsurge.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: EdSurge renewal — initial order form and a couple MSA asks

Kimberly/Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clean redline. A few notes from our side after internal review: 

1) Indemnity: we cannot accept a carveout that shifts IP risk to us for pre-existing integrations; proposed compromise: customer will warrant that customer-provided third-party model weights or plugins are properly licensed, and Redwood will remain liable for Redwood-delivered model code. That keeps allocation balanced.

2) Data residency: we appreciate the carve for legal holds. For routine archival exports, we'd prefer an API-based encrypted export. We agree to a modest export fee but need the fee cap to be spelled out (suggest $1,500 per export).

3) SLA credits: we can accept Redwood's standard SLO exhibit if there is language confirming we have a single point of contact for incident escalation (we'll add the incident manager in the order form).

I've attached EdSurge_CounterRedline_v1.docx and started a DocuSign envelope for the updated order form (link below). We'd like to get this executed by 10/29 to line up with our fiscal close.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/edgsign/abc123

— EdSurge Legal (on behalf of Sara Lopez)

- Indemnity compromise: Kimberly, please accept the proposed warranty split (customer warrants licensing for customer-provided artifacts) and we'll flag in the MSA notes. If Kim has a hard stop, call me before EOD.
- Export fee: Ben, can we accept the $1,500 export fee cap and bake into the order form? If so, update the pricing appendix and return a final order form for DocuSign.
- Incident contact: Naomi, please add a named incident manager and include a short contact block in Exhibit E.

Sara/legal: if you can confirm acceptance of the indemnity wording and the export fee cap, we'll update the redline and ping DocuSign. Our target remains to have the finalized DocuSign envelope by 10/26 so procurement can route prior to your fiscal close.
